chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Yaqoub ibn Salim, from a man, from Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who is healthy and grateful, for him from the recompense is [what is] for the afflicted and patient; and the giver who is grateful, for him from the recompense is like the deprived and contented.

key_terms.الْمُعَافَى: The one who is healthy or free from illness

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual equivalence between health and illness in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of spiritual equity, asserting that the quality of one's worship, rather than the external circumstances, determines divine reward. It highlights that a healthy believer's gratitude yields the same merit as a sick believer's patience, and a wealthy person's grateful giving equals the poor person's contentment. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on internal states (khulus) and the transformative power of gratitude (shukr) in elevating one's spiritual station regardless of material or physical conditions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Yaqoub Bin Salim, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, or Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one of good health, the grateful, for him would be from the Recompense what would be from the afflicted (with illness), the patient; and the giver, the grateful, for him would be from the Recompense like the deprived one, the contented’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn Asbat from Ya’qub ibn Salim from a man from abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘

A person in good health who is thankful for it receives the same amount of reward as a person who in an ailing health exercises patience. One who gives (charity) and is thankful (for his ability) receives the same amount of reward as the deprived person who is content.’”
